response.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT c.State AS State, SUM(i.Total) AS StateTotal, COUNT(*) AS InvoiceCount FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate BETWEEN '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.State) SELECT SUM(StateTotal) AS TotalOfStateTotals, AVG(InvoiceCount) AS AvgInvoicesPerState FROM state_totals;

assumptions.assumption: Customers with no state are those whose State is NULL. GROUP BY places all NULL states in one group. Blank-string states are treated as separate states.
The date range is inclusive at both ends, as BETWEEN is. InvoiceDate is stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' text, so BETWEEN compares it as text as the request specifies.
The average is taken over the per-state invoice counts, so each state (including the no-state group) has equal weight. The sum of state totals equals the sum of Total over all matched invoices.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat blank or whitespace-only State values as 'no state', grouping them with NULL states.
alternatives.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT CASE WHEN TRIM(c.State) = '' THEN NULL ELSE c.State END AS State, SUM(i.Total) AS StateTotal, COUNT(*) AS InvoiceCount FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate BETWEEN '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1) SELECT SUM(StateTotal) AS TotalOfStateTotals, AVG(InvoiceCount) AS AvgInvoicesPerState FROM state_totals;
